rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why
rows.answer: Warps let the GPU execute one instruction across many threads efficiently, rather than managing each thread as a fully independent processor. NVIDIA defines a CUDA warp as 32 threads; that’s a hardware execution-group size, not a requirement that your problem have 32 elements. Divergent branches can reduce efficiency because different paths execute with different subsets of threads active, while consecutive memory accesses can often be combined into fewer memory transactions.

rows.name: spoken-why-during-coding-frozen-21
rows.question: Y
rows.answer: If you mean “why use a circular array,” it gives the FIFO a fixed capacity of 17 with constant-time push and pop, without shifting elements or allocating memory. Separate head, tail, and count fields let it use all 17 slots and distinguish empty from full, so overflow can be rejected without changing existing contents. Advancing indices modulo 17 reuses freed slots while preserving FIFO order.

rows.question: Y
rows.answer: Interpreting “Y” as “why”: “unreliable” describes a customer experience, not a single root cause, so changing the service before identifying the failures could solve the wrong problem. Tracing affected orders and comparing promised with actual outcomes helps locate where things break and how many customers are affected. Prioritizing safety and essential-supply interruptions first limits the most serious harm, then frequency and impact help decide which recurring problem to fix next.
